evidence: The line opens after the clef and key signature with a short beamed run of repeated E4 notes before the first bar line. This matches the closing repeated-E figure of bar 70. The next bar holds eight 32nd groups: E, then A, then F, then higher B groups. This is bar 71, with the B tremolos written out. After the second bar line come four groups of repeated E 32nds, which is the first half of bar 72. The line ends with a curved mark and no bar line, so it stops partway through bar 72.

The line opens with no rests, just four groups of repeated A3 32nds, which reads as the tail of bar 85's run (its rests and first notes were on the previous line). After the bar line come eight groups of 32nds with cresc.; the first group sits lower (A3) and the rest higher (A4), matching bar 86. After the next bar line, marked f, only four groups of repeated A4 appear before the line ends, so it breaks partway through bar 87. This reading assumes the copyist wrote the tremolos out as 32nds.

The first bar has four tremolo groups all at the same high pitch (A4), which matches bar 87 rather than bar 86, since bar 86 opens on the lower A3. The next bar, with tremolo groups followed by single short notes and rests, corresponds to bar 88 (E4 E4 E4, rest), though the copyist writes it differently. Bar 89 follows as rests around paired A3 8ths, then paired D4 8ths. The line closes on bar 90, with rests around paired B3 8ths and then paired E4 8ths, followed by a bar line at the end of the staff.

First bar: marked p, three slurred quarters falling by step and then a quarter rest, matching bar 60 (F3, E3, D3). The next bar is marked f with the dotted 16th-32nd figure, matching bar 61. Last bar: marked p, a 16th rest, then sharped E4 16ths, a low E#3 eighth and a 16th run ending in an eighth plus two 16ths, matching bar 67. It closes with a bar line.

The line opens with four dotted 16ths and a trilled group (A3 F3 G3 A3 | B3 C4 B3), then an A3 8th, an 8th rest and a quarter rest. That matches bar 68, since bar 67's matching figure is followed by A3 F3 instead of rests. Next come the sharped high 16ths (D#4 D4 D4) of bar 69, the descending run to E2 (bar 70), and the tremolo-repeated E figures of bars 71–73. After the last barline, the line ends with E2 8ths followed by 16ths, which is the beginning of bar 74.

The line opens with two rising 32nd-note groups and no bar line before them. These match the second half of bar 35 (E4 F4 G4 A4 B4 C5 D#5 E5 / G4…F5), so the line starts partway into bar 35. After the first bar line come bar 36's 32nd run, its 16ths and the trilled D5 quarter, then the repeat sign. The line closes after the bar line following bar 39's D5 C5 D5 B4 32nds. It ends with the octave 32nd groups of bar 40 (A4/A5, B4/B5, C5/C6, D5/D6…), written as abbreviated repeated notes.

The line opens with the broken-octave 32nd-note groups and grace-note turn of bar 40. It then has bar 41's two grace-note figures, the A–G# eighths and the G quarter, with the G–F pickup before the bar line. Next come bars 42–43, each starting with an F grace note. The line continues with bar 44's octave 32nd groups and its grace-note figures. It ends with the opening A-grace figures of bar 45, which the next line completes.

The opening notes before the first bar line are the end of bar 43. After that bar line come eight 4-note 32nd groups (low note plus repeated upper octave) rising and falling, matching bar 44 (D–E–F–G–F–E–D pattern). Next are the grace-note figures of bars 45–46, then the repeated rest + D4-F4-A4 arpeggio figures of bars 47–48. The line ends still inside these arpeggio groups (B4 over D4/F4) of bar 49, before its closing B4–A4 quarters.

The line opens with two quarter notes before the first bar line, matching the end of bar 49 (B4, A4 quarters). Next comes the sharped quarter (G#4) that begins bar 50, followed by bars 51–52 with their grace-note 32nd figures. Then three bars of 16th arpeggio groups with trilled repeated notes (bars 53–55). After the last bar line there is only the opening F5-D5-A4-D5 group with its trilled F5s, so the line ends partway through bar 56.

The line opens, with no bar line, on two short notes that match the tail of bar 10 (A4 quarter, A5 8th). Next comes the abbreviated 32nd-note arpeggio figure marked p, which is bar 11. The bars that follow match bar 12 (grace note and trill figure), bar 14 (32nd run with F#4) and bars 15–16. The line ends at the double bar after bar 17, whose closing notes are C5 8th., C4 16th, a natural-marked B3 quarter and the A3 half note.

The line opens mid-bar with a dotted quarter and an eighth under 'cresc.' (G5 dotted quarter, B5 eighth, the second half of bar 38). Then come a bar of eight slurred eighths (bar 39), a dotted quarter, an eighth and two quarters marked f (bar 40), a bar with a grace note (bar 41), and three identical eighth-note bars marked ff (bars 42–44). After that is a pp bar of quarter, two eighths and two quarters (bar 45). The line closes with a quarter followed by six eighths marked ff (bar 46), ending at a bar line.

The line opens with a low two-note chord as a half note, then a quarter and a dotted-eighth/sixteenth figure before the first bar line. This matches the A3+G4 half and A4 figures of bar 86. The following eighth-note arpeggio is bar 87, and the next chord half with the pp F5 figure is bar 88. Bars 89–91 follow as the G5/Bb5/Bb4 and A4/F5 eighth-plus-rest patterns. The line ends after A5 rest A4 rest with no closing bar line, which is the first half of bar 92.

The line opens with an eighth note, then rests, then a sharped 32nd group (D#4 D4 D4 D4). This is the F4 8th, rests and D#4 32nds that end bar 16, so the line starts partway through bar 16. After the first bar line come eight 32nd groups: E's, G's, A#-A-A-A, then a natural A and repeated A's, matching bar 17. After the second bar line are four repeated-note groups (G, G, then the D#/D level) under 'cresc.', which match bar 18's tremolo quarters. The line ends with a custos and no bar 20 sixteenth figures, so it ends in bar 18.

The line opens with four beats of written-out 32nds, low E then G and A, which matches bar 17 (8 E4s, G4s, A#4 A4 A4 A4, then the A4 tremolos written out); bar 16's ending is not on this line. Next come 8 beats of 32nds, with naturals before the D group and the following group: bar 18 (G G D# D) then bar 19 (E, G/A, A, A). After the last bar line are two beamed groups of dotted 16ths (G G A F G A G F) and a slur running off the line, so bar 20 begins here and is finished on the next line.

The line has two complete bars, each holding eight beamed four-note groups of 32nd notes on one repeated pitch (G4). Each pair of groups is a written-out quarter tremolo, so each bar is four G4 tremolo quarters. This matches bars 32 and 33 exactly. Bar 31 is ruled out because it opens with rests and four 32nd notes. Bar 34 is ruled out because it changes to D#5 and D5. The final barline closes bar 33.

The line opens with a sharped tremolo note (D#5), followed by repeated-note tremolos and then the figure E5 8th, 16th rest, D5 16th, E5 8th, 16th rest, F4 16th, E5 8th before the first barline. This matches bar 34, though the copy shows four tremolo groups where the edition has two. After that barline come G4 8th / D#5 16th / E5 and then G4 8th and rest pairs, which is bar 35. The line ends after the second barline with G4 8th, rest, and a beamed G4 16th–8th–16th group, the start of bar 36, which is completed on the next line.

The line opens after the clef with a sharp and four written-out 32nd groups (a half note): the E#4 half-note tremolo that ends bar 50, with no bar line before it. The next bar has F (2 groups), a natural then E (2 groups), and a sharp then D# (4 groups), which matches bar 51. After the bar line come two groups of E and a natural before D: the start of bar 52. The line ends there, before bar 52's C4 half note.

The line opens with 16 thirty-second notes and no bar line before them, so it begins halfway through a bar. This matches the second half of bar 50, the written-out E#4 half-note tremolo. The full bar of 32 thirty-seconds that follows fits bar 51 (F4 quarter, E4 quarter, D#4 half). The final group of 16 thirty-seconds runs to the line's end without a closing bar line, so it is the first half of bar 52 (E4 quarter, D4 quarter). Caveat: the pitches in the image are hard to read, so I matched mainly on rhythm and bar-line placement. Bars 51–53 would fit the same pattern equally well.

The line opens with 16 32nd notes (four beamed groups of C-C-C-C, D-D-D-D, C-C-D-D, C-C-B-B), then a bar line. That is a half bar, so it must be the second half of bar 56, after the tremolo D4 half note. Next comes a full bar of 32 32nd notes, which is bar 57. The line then ends after 16 more 32nd notes (C-C-D-D-C-C-B-B twice), the first half of bar 58; the C4 eighth and rests continue on the next line.

After the clef and key signature, the line opens with a whole-bar rest, which is bar 84. Next comes a quarter rest and an 8th rest followed by pp 32nd-note groups on C4, which is bar 85. After a bar line, one low C4 group leads into higher C5 groups under 'cresc.', which is bar 86. After the f and the bar line, the line ends with repeated high C5 32nd groups, matching the start of bar 87.

The line opens with two beamed groups of tremolo-style sixteenths before the first bar line. That matches the tail of bar 30, whose tremolo quarters end ...A, G, A. Each of the next two full bars holds four beamed groups alternating B with G/A, matching the B B B B G A G A pattern of bars 31 and 32. The line ends at a bar line after the second of these bars.

The line opens with one full bar of written-out tremolo (B B B B / G A G A pattern in four beamed groups) closed by a barline, which matches bar 33. The second bar has rests, matching bar 34. Next come a rest and three descending quarters marked pp, matching bar 35's rest and E E E. The line ends with a sharped whole note, D#4, which is bar 36. The final squiggle reads as a custos or flourish rather than bar 37's notes.

The opening slurred half notes (D#5 then D♮5) match bar 113, and the bar line after them leads into the first bar of sixteenths over E4 tremolo, which is bar 114. A third half note before that first bar line has no counterpart in the edition's bar 113, but it does not change the start. The line ends with a full bar of four sixteenth groups (bar 115), then a bar with only two groups and two E4 tremolos (bar 116), cut off partway and completed on the next line.

The line opens mid-bar with two 16th groups (C5 then D5) over low E4s, with no bar line before them. This matches the second half of bar 116. The next full bar has four C-D-C-D 16th groups over E4s, which is bar 117. Next comes a quarter note, rests and a low E4 (bar 118), then a rest and three A4 quarters marked pp (bar 119). The line closes on the G4 whole note (bar 120) before the final bar line.

First bar 6: the line opens with a very high E6 followed by repeated E5 eighths marked 'dol:'. These lead into the slurred D#5–D♮5 and the falling sixteenths. Bar 7 follows: a trilled F4 and then an E-minor arpeggio. Bar 8 starts on a high B5 and continues with repeated B4s marked 'Dolis:' and A#4–A♮4. Last bar 9: the final bar holds the 32nd-note figures starting on D#4 (rising groups, then two falling 32nd runs). It closes with a bar line at the right edge.

The line opens with a single upbeat quarter (pp) before the first bar line. That matches the one-beat bar 26 after the repeat. Next comes a half plus quarter under a slur (bar 27). Then quarter, rest and three eighths (bar 28), three quarters (bar 29), and three half–quarter bars (30–32). The dotted-eighth/sixteenth figure followed by quarters including a sharped note is bar 33 (G F E D#). The closing quarter just before the final bar line is the resolution to E, so I read the line as ending in bar 34. That last call is the least certain: the copy shows a quarter where the edition prints E4 as a half, so this may be a first-ending form of the bar.

The line opens with a half rest, a low A3 quarter and a high G5/E5, which is bar 98 (bar 97's whole rest is not on this line). This pattern repeats with the paired D4+A4+F5 chords (bars 99 and 103) and the A4+C#5 chord followed by rests (bars 100 and 104), with a whole rest between them (bar 101). The line ends with the C#5 chord and rests running through bar 105's rest; the next bar begins after the final bar line. The copyist's bar lines are offset from the edition's around the C#5 chords, so the end point is approximate.

The line opens with a half rest followed by a half-note B4 marked 'dol.', which matches bar 22. Next comes B4 then #A4 (bar 23, 'pocof.'), then two B4 halves (bar 24, 'p:'). It ends with #A4 then natural A4 (bar 25), followed by the final barline.

The line closes with a final double bar after a bar of two eighths, a group of 32nds and a quarter under a fermata. That matches bar 29 (E4 E4, A4-G4-F4-E4 32nds, D4 quarter, rest, D4 quarter). Counting back over the two internal bar lines gives two earlier bars. Each begins with an eighth rest followed by beamed eighths, as bars 27 and 28 do. The opening pp segment, eighth rest then the descending eighths, is therefore bar 27. This reading is tentative because the handwriting is hard to resolve note by note.

The line opens partway through bar 6: the copyist writes the A4 quarter, the dotted-8th/16th figure (looks like an ornament) and the E4 quarter, with no bar line before them. Then come bar 7 (four quarters E-D-E-B) and bar 8 (quarter, rest, quarter before the repeat sign). After the repeat is the pickup of bar 9. Bar 10 is rest, rest, D4 marked pp. Bar 11 is a half note plus rest, bar 12 is rest, rest, D4, and bar 13 is a half note plus rest, ending at the final bar line.

The line opens with four groups of eight 32nds up to the first barline. The last group ends with a sharp, matching bar 29's ending (…F5 D#5 E5), so the line starts at bar 29. The next segment has two 32nd groups, then 16ths with a trill marked 'dolce' and sharps (F F G A B# C D# E), which is bar 30. After the second barline, the sharped rising 16ths (E#5…B#5 C6) fall to repeated B/C 16ths with a rest and then reach the final barline, which is bar 31.

Working backwards from the end: the second-to-last bar is a rest, E3, rest, G3 (bar 75). The last bar, a low C3 quarter followed by rests, is bar 76. Before bar 75 come two bars of rest, E3, rest, F3 (bars 73–74). Before those is E4, low C3, rest, F3, C4 (bar 72). The two opening bars repeat the E4 / G3+E4 / D4 / G3+B3 double-stop pattern, so they are bars 70 and 71. Bar 69 has the same pattern, but it is ruled out by counting back from bar 72.

The line opens, after the clef and key signature, with a rest, two repeated quarters and a rest marked p. This matches bar 77 (rest, D4, D4, rest), and bars 78 and 79 follow, the latter marked cresc. A half note plus rest gives bar 80. After the ff come four short groups: quarter, dotted pair, quarters; then half plus quarters; then the same two patterns again. These correspond to the material of bars 81–84, although the edition's grouping of 81–84 does not line up exactly with the manuscript's bar divisions. The line closes with a half note and two quarters, matching bar 84 (F4 half, then A4/F4 quarters), so the last bar is less certain than the first.

The line opens with a high group of A4 32nds followed by low A3 and C4 groups and a natural-marked D group: bar 71 from its first note, with no G4 pickup from bar 70. The next bar, after the bar line, has repeated C4 32nds then written-out G3 tremolo groups, matching bar 72 (cresc.). After the second bar line come the A3 tremolo, a C4 group and a natural-marked D group, then the line breaks off with a custos. So the line ends partway through bar 73.

The line opens, after the repeat sign and key signature, with rests and then the sharp E (E#4) followed by the 16ths F-A-G-F and E-E, which is bar 67. Bars 68 and 69 follow, with bar 69 again starting with rests and then D#4. The line ends after E-G-F-E 16ths, then #D-D, which is the start of bar 70.

The line opens with the grace-note and dotted-16th/32nd figures of bar 5. Next come the eight eighths of bar 6 (one eighth plus a beamed three, twice), then bar 7: the 'poco f' low A3 quarter, G#3 and A3 half on ledger lines. After the repeat sign are bar 8 (half rest, B4 quarter, two B4 eighths, pp) and bar 9 (eighths alternating with rests). The line ends with the pp alternating E4–G4 sixteenth figures that begin bar 10.

The line opens with four beamed 16ths (C4 E4 D#4 C4), then sharped B#3, B3, C4 and rests, which is bar 14. Next comes rest, rest, A#3, then the 16ths B D# C B and the 8ths A3 A3, which is bar 15. The last segment has the 16ths B D# C B, sharped A#3 A3, and repeated B3s, which is bar 16; it ends at the closing barline.

The line opens with three quarter notes (A4 G4 B4), which is bar 23. Next comes a quarter, a dotted 8th + 16th figure and a trilled quarter (A4 F4 D4 B3), which is bar 24. It ends on a half note with a fermata (C4), bar 25, followed by the repeat sign. Bar 26's rest does not appear on this line.

The line opens with two matching bars, each holding a half rest followed by a four-note 16th run and an 8th note; these are bars 18 and 19. Next comes a measure-rest bar marked with a '2' above it, covering bars 20–21. Then come the 8th-note figures with a sharp (C#4 E G, then C E G), which is bar 22. The final bar, rest followed by A A E E, D F, is bar 23, closed by a barline.

First bar 48: the line opens with a single 8th note (A4) followed by rests. Then come three beamed groups marked with flats, matching the Bb4 16th + D4/F4 32nd figures that end bar 48. After the bar line, a flat-marked 8th (Bb4), a rest and the 'P:' repeated D4 8ths match bar 49. Last bar 50: after the next bar line, marked 'Poco f', four beamed 32nd-note groups (D4×8, B3×8) and a half note with a tremolo stroke (E#4) match the start of bar 50, so the line ends inside bar 50.

The line opens with the end of bar 78: D5/D4 figures before the first bar line. Bar 79 is next, ending on the D4 half note marked 'ten'. Bar 80's rest and 16th run (marked 'pocof') follows. Then comes bar 81, with tremolo 32nd groups and the low A3 F4 C4 B3 eighths. The line closes with two bars of low C4 eighths alternating with rests, which are bars 82 and 83, ending at the final bar line.

The line opens with the ornamented G4 bar, followed by the D#4–rest–D4–F4 bar, then the ornamented A4/D#4/F4 bar, the E4 half plus half rest (bar 20) and a whole-bar rest (bar 21). That places the opening ornamented bar at 17. After the rests come the pp whole note F4 (22), E4 with C♮4 (23), B3 with the long F4 (24) and the two halves (25), which closes the line.

The line opens with two beamed eighths, then an eighth, an eighth rest, a dotted quarter and an eighth before the first barline. This matches the end of bar 132 (C4 D4 | D4, rest, D4 dotted quarter, F4). The final measure has A eighths separated by rests, which is bar 136. One more A eighth sits at the right edge with no barline before the line ends; that is the first note of bar 137 (A4 8th), so the line ends partway through bar 137.

First bar: after the clef and key signature come a quarter note, a quarter rest and a slurred run of 8ths ending in a sharp. This matches bar 53 (C4, rest, C4 B3 B3 A#3). The next bar is a quarter, a rest and four rising 8ths (bar 54), then a quarter, a rest and two chords (bar 55). Last bar: three bars of a half chord plus two quarter chords (bars 56–58) follow. The line ends with a chord, then running notes, closed by a barline, which is bar 59.

The line opens partway through a bar with a group of four 16ths followed by a short figure. This matches the second half of bar 45 (F4 D4 D4 D4 16ths, then D4 8th). After the first bar line come the rest–16th pairs marked p., which fit bar 46 (rest 16th / F4 16th repeated), followed by its beamed 16th run. After the second bar line come two 16ths and then rest–16th pairs, which fit bar 47 (E4 E4, then rest/E4 pairs). The line closes with the f. figure and a final bar line, read as the end of bar 47; that last figure did not clearly match bar 47's printed F4 and A3 8ths, so the end point is less certain than the start.

First bar: the first segment (a ♮ note, repeated eighths, a note and an ending rest) fits bar 14 (C4 quarter, C4 C4, A♮3 quarter, A3 8th, rest 8th). The next segment opens with a flatted quarter followed by eighths, matching bar 15 (Bb3 quarter, B3 B3, G3 G3 A3 C4). The third segment has eighth rests and a sharped final note, matching bar 16 (…C4 A3 F#4). Last bar: the final segment of four repeated notes ending in a half note matches bar 17 (E4 8th, E4 quarter, E4 8th, E4 half), followed by the closing repeat sign.

The line opens with an 8th rest, a sharped D4 and repeated D4 eighths, then the high B4 half note (marked with a natural) that ends bar 11. After the first bar line come repeated B3 sixteenths under 'ff', which is bar 12. After the second bar line come rests, then B#3 and the C-E-D#-C sixteenths followed by two B3 eighths, which is bar 13, ending at the line-end bar line. The opening of bar 11 is hard to read in the hand copy, but it is the only bar before the first bar line that ends with that B4 half note.

The line opens with an eighth rest and three repeated eighths before the first bar line, which matches the second half of bar 9 (rest 8th, A4 A4 A4). The first half of bar 9 is therefore on the previous line. Bar 10 follows (eighth rest, quarter, quarter, three eighths, marked cresc.), then bar 11 (eighth rest plus a run of repeated A's, marked f). The line ends with bar 12: four groups of 32nd-note runs, then a single eighth note (E4) and rests, closed by the final bar line.

The line opens with a low half-note chord followed by a quarter and a dotted-8th/16th figure, matching bar 85 (A3+F4 half, then D5 quarter, D5 8th., D5 16th). The next bar is an abbreviated broken-chord figure (bar 86), and the chord was identified by counting back from the following low sharped half note, which is the C#4 that opens bar 87. After bar 88's abbreviated figure and its F4 quarter, F4 8th. with two 32nds comes the last barline. The line then ends with an 8th, an 8th rest and a dotted 8th with 32nds, which is the first half of bar 89.

After the key-change naturals, the first bar holds a full 8-eighth figure E3 | D4 C4 E3 | F3 D4 C4 F3. Of the three identical bars (73–75), only bar 73 is followed by exactly two more of the same figure before the D3-figure bar 75 and the short C3 bar 76, so the line starts at bar 73. It then runs through the p whole B2 (77), A2 (78), G2/C2 (79) and F2 + rest (80). It ends with the ff F2 half followed by two quarters (bar 81) at the final barline.
